question: Can the freely generated recurrent mean retain the native high-state spatial and feedback behavior when the additional independent recurrent residual approximation is omitted?
motivation: Source-temporal audit shows the independent white residual exaggerates filtered variance; AR64 fails to represent the source-derived residual spectrum. A leading-mean diagnostic separates free recurrent mean dynamics from the added residual approximation before constructing a more complicated covariance model.
design: One1s trajectory,40000 physicaltargets x64 numericalreplicas, from samecomplete72s nativehighstate. Exact individualthresholds, original delays/weights, percellfixednu and Poisson externalcounts; Z/K held, membrane/synapse/ref/M/G evolve. Mean recurrent arrivals are generated by the models own source probabilities. Set only added recurrent fluctuationvariance tozero; no neural teacher forcing, phaseperiod, biological parameter or amplitude fitting.
pairing: MainGaussian and externalPoisson RNG streams identical to completed Poisson-external assay. Gaussian recurrent draws are still consumed but do not contribute. Countlaw, complete initialstate and mean operators remain identical.
limits: This deliberately omits finite-network recurrent residuals and their source correlations. It is a leading mean-input diagnostic, not a claim they vanish in the native system. Retaining one conditional state would permit further independent correspondence and finite-noise checks, not certify a stablebranch or entireloop.
stop: One1s only with the same native relevance guards; no automatic parameter, order, horizon, root or bifurcation calculation.
